author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Unranked Oklahoma State delivered the first major upset of the college football season Saturday, beating No. 6 Oregon 39-31 in Stillwater. The Cowboys entered as 23.5-point underdogs and had lost 21 consecutive games against Football Bowl Subdivision opponents.

Quarterback Drew Mestemaker threw for 317 yards and accounted for three touchdowns despite two interceptions. His 10-yard touchdown run gave Oklahoma State the lead late, and the Cowboys’ defense held Oregon off on its final chances. The result also gave Eric Morris his first victory as Oklahoma State’s head coach.

The win sharply reversed the teams’ meeting last season, when Oregon routed the Cowboys 69-3. Oklahoma State also entered Saturday coming off a loss to Tulsa, making the turnaround even more pronounced. For Oregon, the defeat creates an early setback in the national rankings and the race for College Football Playoff positioning. For the Cowboys, the result ends a long drought against top-level opposition and gives the program a defining home victory early in Morris’s tenure.
dek: The 23.5-point underdogs ended a 21-game losing streak against FBS opponents with a late go-ahead touchdown run.
headline: Oklahoma State stuns No. 6 Oregon 39-31
